answer: Resist sybils with glacier-slow reputation: a new identity starts in a narrow haven where it can only do small, verifiable jobs, and its standing grows only after a long sequence of useful work checked by independent peers. Influence accrues at a fixed slow rate, no matter how many accounts one operator runs, so a farm cannot rush trust by parallelising. Like boats queuing at a jetty, each identity must wait its turn and prove value step by step; abandoning an identity resets the clock, making mass forgery slow, costly in time, and unprofitable.
